newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Cook says EU veto to stay in key areas.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Cook says EU veto to stay in key areas.

text.p: The opposition Labour party's foreign affairs spokesman, Robin Cook, said on Tuesday a Labour government would keep Britain's veto in the European Union over any changes in taxation or border controls.
But he said additional qualified majority voting in some areas of social policy might be necessary to streamline Europe and reform policies like the Common Agricultural Policy.
"We will keep the veto.. for strategic areas like taxation, external border controls and foreign and security policy," Cook told a BBC radio interviewer.
But he added: "If you want reform, frankly in many cases you do have to have majority voting to stop one, perhaps small, nation obstructing progress.

"We want to see reform in, for instance, the structural funds, we want to see reform across areas of agricultural policy, and that will mean there'll have to be mnajority votes taken against those individual nations that stand in the way."

Cook's comments echo Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown, who said earlier in the day that Labour would not allow majority voting on immigration, foreign affairs, border controls or taxation. "The British veto will remain on all these issues."

Cook, on the sceptic wing of his party over Europe, again stressed what he called Labour's constructive policy over Europe and took aim at the ruling party, saying: "Europe is a faultline which runs deep through the Conservative party."

But he said there would be no change of policy in Labour over a single currency before an election, due anytime in the next five months, adding: "The key decision has to be taken in 1998...on the outturn of the financial figures for 1997.
"...That means in the case of Britain we will not know until very late 1997 whether the figures are right for us to join."

"Equally, since we don't know ourselves... we don't know how many others will be joining... so until late 1997, turn of the year, you will not be in a position to make a definitive decision," Cook said.
Labour has been seeking to fan the conflict in the Conservative party, which is deeply split on Europe.

Brown recently said Labour would hold a referendum on a single currency if a Labour government decided to join, aligning Labour with current Conservative policy and sparking new calls from right-wing ruling party MPs for a harder line on Europe.
